blocks.text: The accusative case is a peculiar case in Russian, as it makes a distinction that other cases do not. Specifically, if a masculine word denotes an inanimate thing ('table', 'chair', etc), then it remains the same as the nominative. If, however, a masculine word denotes a person or animal ('man', 'son', 'cow', etc), then the case uses the endings of the *genitive case*. For plurals in the accusative, no matter what gender the word, they are also split: any plural word that's inanimate is identical to its nominative plural form, while animate plural words follow the rules for the genitive plural. Some examples highlighting this distinction are as follows:

items: Этот стул коричневый. - Nominative of an inanimate noun
Я де́лал стул. - Accusative of the noun
Этот кот любит меня. - Nom. of an animate noun
Я люблю этого кота. - Acc. of the noun
Эти женщины любят меня. - Nom. of an animate, plural, feminine noun
Я люблю этих женщин. - Acc. of the noun

blocks.text: So, masculine nouns denoting inanimate objects in the accusative case are the same as in the nominative case. If they're animated nouns, they follow the genitive rules, which are: add **-а**, and replace **-й** and **-ь** with **-я**.
Neuter nouns, regardless of animation, also keep their nominative forms in the accusative case.
Feminine words are the only words to have their own accusative ending: **-а** becomes **-у**, and **-я** becomes **-ю**. Feminine nouns ending in the soft sign **-ь** do not change.

To form the plural of an inanimate word, use the nominative rules: add or replace with **-ы** or **-и**, and neuter nouns change **-o** to **-а** and **-e** to **-я**. If the word is animate, regardless of gender, use the genitive plural: drop **-а** and **-о**, convert or append ending consonants with **-ов**, **-ев**, or **-ей**, and replace **-я** with **-ь** or **-й**.
This summary table splits the masculine and plural forms into two sections, the left being the inanimate form, the right being the animate form.

Adjectives change to fit the noun they modify, taking on their noun's gender, number, and case. This also includes animation: adjectives modifying inanimate masculine nouns keep their nominative form (**ый**, **ий**, and **ой**), while animate masculine adjectives take on their genitive form (**ого** and **его**).
Neuter adjectives also keep their nominative form (**ое** and **ее**).
Feminine adjectives in the accusative case have the ending (**ую** and **юю**) - this is easy to remember, as it's the two endings of feminine nouns in the accusative.

Plural adjectives take on their nominative form (**ые** and **ие**) when modifying inanimate nouns, and their genitive form (**ых** and **их**) when modifying animate nouns, as you might have guessed.

items: We are listening to the latest music.
Купи, пожалуйста, свежие фрукты.-  Please, buy fresh fruits.

blocks.text: Notice that the third-person singular masculine and neuter pronouns are the same word, **его**, and, like the genitive adjectival ending, it is pronounced *ye-VOH*. The third-person personal pronouns, **его, её**, and **их**, are the same as those in the genitive.
From the Wikibooks Russian textbook (CC BY-SA 4.0).
Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Она открыла сумочку и достала ___ (чековый, acc. sg. f.) книжку.
exercises.prompt: She opened her purse and took out her chequebook.
exercises.why: **чековый → чековую** (acc. sg. f., agreeing with книжку). Declines like новый (A. новую). Ending -ая → -ую.  — DLI Grammar Reference Book; OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Том был вовлечён в ___ (уличный, acc. sg. f.) стычку.
exercises.prompt: Tom was involved in a street brawl.
exercises.why: **уличный → уличную** (acc. sg. f., agreeing with стычку). Declines like новый (A. новую). Ending -ая → -ую.  — DLI Grammar Reference Book; OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Том запер дверь на ___ (висячий, acc. sg. m.) замок.
exercises.prompt: Tom padlocked the door.
exercises.why: **висячий → висячий** (acc. sg. m., agreeing with замок). Declines like хороший (A. anim. = G., inan. = N). No change of ending: here the accusative is the same as the nominative.  — DLI Grammar Reference Book; OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Наука привнесла в ___ (наш, acc. sg. f.) жизнь множество изменений.
exercises.prompt: Science has brought about many changes to our lives.
exercises.why: **наш → нашу** (acc. sg. f., agreeing with жизнь). Declines like наш. Ending -а → -у.  — DLI Grammar Reference Book; OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Конденсатор позволяет току протекать через ___ (пустой, acc. sg. n.) пространство.
exercises.prompt: A capacitor allows current to flow through empty space.
exercises.why: **пустой → пустое** (acc. sg. n., agreeing with пространство). Declines like новый (A. новое; the masculine nominative ends in -ой, not -ый). No change of ending: here the accusative is the same as the nominative.  — DLI Grammar Reference Book; OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Я не люблю играть в ___ (игровой, acc. pl.) автоматы.
exercises.prompt: I don't like to play on the slot machines.
exercises.why: **игровой → игровые** (acc. pl., agreeing with автоматы). Declines like новый (A. anim. = G., inan. = N; the masculine nominative ends in -ой, not -ый). No change of ending: here the accusative is the same as the nominative.  — DLI Grammar Reference Book; OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Закат иногда окрашивает небо в ___ (красный, acc. sg. m.) цвет.
exercises.prompt: The sunset sometimes turns the sky red.
exercises.why: **красный → красный** (acc. sg. m., agreeing with цвет). Declines like новый (A. anim. = G., inan. = N). No change of ending: here the accusative is the same as the nominative.  — DLI Grammar Reference Book; OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Том проглядел ___ (мой, acc. sg. f.) ошибку.
exercises.prompt: Tom overlooked my mistake.
exercises.why: **мой → мою** (acc. sg. f., agreeing with ошибку). Declines like мой. Ending -я → -ю.  — DLI Grammar Reference Book; OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Он вылил ___ (холодный, acc. sg. f.) воду на себя.
exercises.prompt: He poured cold water over himself.
exercises.why: **холодный → холодную** (acc. sg. f., agreeing with воду). Declines like новый (A. новую). Ending -ая → -ую.  — DLI Grammar Reference Book; OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: В ___ (главный, acc. sg. m.) офис нагрянула полиция.
exercises.prompt: The main office was raided by the police.
exercises.why: **главный → главный** (acc. sg. m., agreeing with офис). Declines like новый (A. anim. = G., inan. = N). No change of ending: here the accusative is the same as the nominative.  — DLI Grammar Reference Book; OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Художник передала свои работы в ___ (общественный, acc. sg. n.) достояние.
exercises.prompt: The artist released her works into the public domain.
exercises.why: **общественный → общественное** (acc. sg. n., agreeing with достояние). Declines like новый (A. новое). No change of ending: here the accusative is the same as the nominative.  — DLI Grammar Reference Book; OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Ты взял ___ (тёплый, acc. sg. f.) одежду?
exercises.prompt: Did you bring any warm clothes?
exercises.why: **тёплый → тёплую** (acc. sg. f., agreeing with одежду). Declines like новый (A. новую). Ending -ая → -ую.  — DLI Grammar Reference Book; OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Борцуны за ___ (социальный, acc. sg. f.) справедливость у меня уже в печёнках сидят.
exercises.prompt: I'm getting fed up with SJWs.
exercises.why: **социальный → социальную** (acc. sg. f., agreeing with справедливость). Declines like новый (A. новую). Ending -ая → -ую.  — DLI Grammar Reference Book; OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Они нас за ___ (дойный, acc. pl.) коров держат.
exercises.prompt: They're taking us for cash cows.
exercises.why: **дойный → дойных** (acc. pl., agreeing with коров). Declines like новый (A. anim. = G., inan. = N). Ending -ые → -ых.  — DLI Grammar Reference Book; OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Просто невозможно доделать ___ (курсовой, acc. sg. f.) работу к завтрашнему дню!
exercises.prompt: It is impossible for me to finish my term paper by tomorrow.
exercises.why: **курсовой → курсовую** (acc. sg. f., agreeing with работу). Declines like новый (A. новую; the masculine nominative ends in -ой, not -ый). Ending -ая → -ую.  — DLI Grammar Reference Book; OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Я ищу ___ (съёмный, acc. sg. f.) квартиру.
exercises.prompt: I'm looking for an apartment to rent.
exercises.why: **съёмный → съемную** (acc. sg. f., agreeing with квартиру). Declines like новый (A. новую). Ending -ая → -ую.  — DLI Grammar Reference Book; OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Я думаю, что мы должны совершить ___ (повторный, acc. sg. f.) попытку.
exercises.prompt: I think that we should try again.
exercises.why: **повторный → повторную** (acc. sg. f., agreeing with попытку). Declines like новый (A. новую). Ending -ая → -ую.  — DLI Grammar Reference Book; OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Он слеп на ___ (левый, acc. sg. m.) глаз.
exercises.prompt: He's blind in his left eye.
exercises.why: **левый → левый** (acc. sg. m., agreeing with глаз). Declines like новый (A. anim. = G., inan. = N). No change of ending: here the accusative is the same as the nominative.  — DLI Grammar Reference Book; OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Ты когда-нибудь выписывал ___ (англоязычный, acc. sg. f.) газету?
exercises.prompt: Have you ever subscribed to any English language newspaper?
exercises.why: **англоязычный → англоязычную** (acc. sg. f., agreeing with газету). Declines like новый (A. новую). Ending -ая → -ую.  — DLI Grammar Reference Book; OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Мой сосед высеивает ___ (новый, acc. sg. f.) траву в своём дворе.
exercises.prompt: My neighbor is planting new grass in his yard.
exercises.why: **новый → новую** (acc. sg. f., agreeing with траву). Declines like новый (A. новую). Ending -ая → -ую.  — DLI Grammar Reference Book; OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).
